verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "I have soreness in my fingers, and my finger, like, the skin on my hands is kind of cracked."
When asked when it started, patient says: "A couple of months ago. Like, three, four months ago."
Patient reports it has worsened and impacts work: "it's gotten to a point where it hurts a lot, and I can't really do my job" and later "the past three days, I haven't been able to go to work."
Doctor asks about itchiness and patient replies: "Yeah, it's itchy. Not all the time, but, yeah, it does get itchy."
On bleeding with scratching: Patient says, "when I scratched it, yes, it has bled sometimes, but... otherwise it hasn't bled on its own."
In past medical history, patient responds: "I have diabetes."
When asked about medications, patient states: "Metformin."
Doctor asks: "Do you have any allergies either to any medications or in general?" but no allergies are given in response anywhere in the transcript, so no allergies are reported.
Family history: Doctor asks, "Family history wise? Is there anything I should be aware of?" Patient answers: "Diabetes as well?"
Patient states: "I do work as a housekeeper."
Patient notes inconsistent glove use: "to be honest, I'm not always very good about wearing gloves."
Patient says: "I switched jobs four months ago."

Doctor and patient discuss association with cleaning products: Doctor says there may be "a reaction between the chemicals... and your skin" and earlier acknowledges "there's definitely maybe a correlation between the two" (housekeeping/cleaning products and symptoms).
Alcohol history: Patient says, "Once a week. A couple of pints. A week?" and doctor summarizes: "so very minimal alcohol there."
Doctor asks, "Do you smoke at all?" Patient: "No."
Doctor assessment: "I think you might have something called dermatitis or contact dermatitis."
Doctor links it to cleaning products: "particularly people in your field who are using cleaning products, not using gloves. Sometimes get a bit of a reaction between the chemicals... and your skin."
Plan includes: "I strongly recommend that you wear gloves when cleaning at all times."
Doctor proposes steroid cream: "we can try some steroid creams to help with inflammation." A prescription is later sent to the pharmacy.
Doctor adds: "as well as some stronger emollients which you really need to kind of coat on throughout the day."

Follow-up instructions: "If it still hasn't got better in about a week to two weeks time, I really want you to come back" and later clarified as "a minimum couple of weeks, 10 days to 14 days" and "if it's getting worse... come back and see me sooner."
Doctor asks: "have you had any other symptoms, such as fever or temperatures" and patient answers "No."
Same question includes nausea; patient replies: "No."
Same question includes vomiting; patient replies: "No."
Doctor asks: "Any problem with your bowels?" and "Any problems with your urine?" Patient answers "No" to both.
